config.documentTitleFull: PETITION FOR EXPUNGEMENT OF A CITY ORDINANCE CONVICTION OR DIVERSION PURSUANT TO K.S.A. 12-4516
config.courtCaption: IN THE MUNICIPAL COURT OF THE CITY OF [CITY OF THE UNDERLYING ORDINANCE VIOLATION — CONFIRM WITH THE COURT], KANSAS

primaryStatutoryAuthority.description: A person convicted of a violation of a city ordinance may petition the convicting municipal court to expunge the conviction and related arrest records; a person who has fulfilled the terms of a diversion agreement based on a city ordinance violation may likewise petition the court. The court sets a hearing and causes notice to be given to the prosecuting attorney and the arresting law enforcement agency, and shall order expungement on three findings: that the petitioner has not been convicted of a felony in the past two years and no such proceeding is pending or being instituted; that the petitioner's circumstances and behaviour warrant expungement; and that expungement is consistent with the public welfare. There is no firearms finding, because a municipal ordinance conviction is not a felony.

Conviction of a city ordinance violation: the petition may be brought once three or more years have elapsed from the latest of satisfying the sentence imposed or discharge from probation, parole or a suspended sentence.
Fulfilled diversion agreement based on a city ordinance violation: the petition may be brought once three or more years have elapsed from the date the terms of the diversion agreement were fulfilled.
An ordinance violation prohibited by K.S.A. 12-16,134(a) or (b) and adopted before July 1, 2014: no elapsed period is stated for this category.

An ordinance violation that would also constitute prostitution under K.S.A. 21-6419 or former K.S.A. 21-3512, where the petitioner can prove coercion caused by the act of another: one year from satisfying the sentence, fulfilling the diversion terms or discharge from supervision.

Five years for an ordinance violation that would also constitute vehicular homicide, driving while cancelled, suspended or revoked, perjury under K.S.A. 8-261a, a fraudulent application under K.S.A. 8-142 Fifth, a felony in which a motor vehicle was used, failing to stop at an accident scene, no motor vehicle liability insurance under K.S.A. 40-3104, or a violation of former K.S.A. 21-3405b.

Five years for an ordinance violation that would also constitute a first violation of K.S.A. 8-1567 (driving under the influence) under (e)(1), and ten years for a second or subsequent violation under (e)(2). Subsection (e) applies to all violations committed on or after July 1, 2006, and the municipal statute has no equivalent of the K.S.A. 21-6614(d)(3) seven-year window.
Identifies the ordinance categories referenced by K.S.A. 12-4516(b), and is carried in the pinned registry authority list for this track.

counselFlags: Court-specific instrument: Kansas has hundreds of municipal courts and no unified municipal forms regime, so the instrument is court-specific even though the mechanism is statewide. Confirm with the convicting municipal court whether it publishes its own expungement form or requires its own process before filing this document.

Charter ordinance risk: some Kansas cities govern expungement by charter ordinance rather than by K.S.A. 12-4516 directly. A bounded sample confirmed that Wichita proceeds under Charter Ordinance No. 224 and publishes its own Motion and Order. Where a city proceeds by charter ordinance, this petition may be the wrong instrument entirely.

The city is never guessed. The city whose ordinance was violated is left as a confirm-with-the-court value in the caption and court name, because naming the wrong municipal court would misdirect the filing.

Waiting periods vary sharply by offence: three years for a conviction under (a)(1) or a fulfilled diversion under (a)(2); no elapsed period for a pre-July-1-2014 ordinance under (b); one year under (c) for a prostitution-equivalent violation where coercion by another is proved; five years for the offences listed in (d); five years for a first DUI-equivalent under (e)(1) and ten years for a second or subsequent one under (e)(2). Confirm which period applies before filing.
The three statutory findings are the court's to make, never the petitioner's to assert. This pleading asks the court to make them; it never states that they have been made.

Notice is the court's act: the court sets the hearing and causes notice to be given to the prosecuting attorney and the arresting law enforcement agency. The participant does not serve anyone, and the prosecuting attorney's position is never asserted.

Kansas municipal verification: K.S.A. 12-4516 as described by the source imposes no verification or notarization requirement and identifies no verification statute. Confirm what the convicting municipal court requires before signing; the source does not specify one.

Filing fee: the source does not establish a filing fee for a K.S.A. 12-4516 conviction or diversion petition. No amount may be stated to a participant; ask the convicting municipal court what it charges.
There is no firearms finding on this track, because a municipal ordinance conviction is not a felony. Do not import the firearms analysis that applies to Kansas district court expungements.

Excluded: a commercial driving-under-the-influence equivalent under K.S.A. 8-2,144 is excluded by K.S.A. 12-4516(f); a petitioner convicted of a felony within the past two years, or against whom such a proceeding is pending or being instituted, is excluded by K.S.A. 12-4516(h)(1). A district court conviction or diversion runs under K.S.A. 21-6614 instead, and an arrest with no municipal conviction and no municipal diversion runs under K.S.A. 12-4516a.
Any pending felony proceeding, any felony conviction within the past two years, and any question about which waiting period applies should trigger attorney review before filing.

registryExcerpt.venue: Statewide statute available in every Kansas municipal court, executed court by court. K.S.A. 12-4516(a)(1) directs a conviction petition to the convicting court, which is the municipal court of the city whose ordinance was violated, and (a)(2) directs a diversion petition to the court. Kansas has hundreds of municipal courts and no unified municipal forms regime, so the instrument is court-specific even though the mechanism is statewide.

caption.detail: Municipal court caption naming the city whose ordinance was violated. The city is deliberately left as a confirm-with-the-court bracket value rather than guessed, because Kansas has hundreds of municipal courts and naming the wrong one would misdirect the filing.

court_party_identity.detail: The sovereign party is the city (Plaintiff), not the State of Kansas — a municipal ordinance prosecution is brought by the city. The movant is the Petitioner. The prosecuting attorney and arresting law enforcement agency are named by role only as the recipients of the court's notice; no position is asserted for either.

title.detail: PETITION FOR EXPUNGEMENT OF A CITY ORDINANCE CONVICTION OR DIVERSION PURSUANT TO K.S.A. 12-4516.

allegations.detail: Facts and case-history allegations built solely from participant-supplied record data, plus the eligibility allegation drawn from the K.S.A. 12-4516 waiting-period text. The three statutory findings are framed as relief requested of the court, never as facts already found.

statutory_basis.detail: K.S.A. 12-4516 and its subsections (a)(1), (a)(2), (b), (c), (d) and (e), plus K.S.A. 12-16,134. Subsection attributions are taken only where the pinned registry makes them; the hearing-and-findings provision is cited to the section generally because the source does not number it.

requested_relief.detail: Expunge the conviction or diversion identified in the Petition and the arrest records related to it — the scope K.S.A. 12-4516 confers and no wider.

verification.detail: Signed declaration only. The source imposes no verification or notarization requirement and identifies no verification statute, so none is asserted (citation null + recorded silence + counsel flag).

signatures.detail: Petitioner signature and date blocks; the judge's signature block on the proposed order stays blank for the court.

proposed_order.detail: Proposed order to expunge, filed with the petition. K.S.A. 12-4516 requires the court to order expungement on the three findings, and the bounded Kansas sample records a municipal Motion and Order practice.

certificate_of_service.detail: Absent by design: the court sets the hearing and causes notice to be given to the prosecuting attorney and the arresting law enforcement agency. The participant serves no one, so the source prescribes no certificate of service.

notice_affidavit.detail: Absent by design: notice is the court's act under K.S.A. 12-4516. The source prescribes no participant notice or affidavit document.

participant_cover_sheet.detail: participant-instructions.md — participant-only completion, signing, court-confirmation and filing guide, separate from the court documents.

filing_instructions.detail: Confirm the convicting municipal court's own practice first, then file the petition and proposed order with that court. The court sets the hearing and gives notice. The filing fee is not established and must be confirmed with the court.
